description: CTU-13 is a dataset of real botnet traffic mixed with normal and background traffic, captured at the Czech Technical University in 2011. It holds thirteen captures, called scenarios, in each of which a specific malware sample was run and used various protocols and actions. Coverage: one university network, 2011. Every scenario was labelled by hand inside bidirectional NetFlow files generated with Argus, with labels for background, botnet, command and control channels and normal traffic; the page advises against the older unidirectional NetFlows. Format and access: for each scenario, the PCAP of the botnet traffic only, the labelled bidirectional NetFlow files (.biargus) and the original executable, downloadable per scenario or as one 1.9 GB archive, with a backup mirror; free. Licence: not stated on the page read; users are asked to cite Garcia et al. (2014), Computers and Security 45, 100-123. Caveats: the full PCAPs with background and normal traffic are withheld for privacy; the traffic is from 2011 and from an enterprise network, not an operational technology network; the archive contains live malware executables. Simulation uses: benchmark traffic for testing detection of compromised hosts, as one input to cyber resilience studies of telecom and control networks. Related records: CIC datasets (data-cic-unb-cybersecurity-datasets) are another widely used intrusion detection collection.
